DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Sewage lagoon at Fugate Mobile Home Park have been leaking across the road for years.  They drain into the woods surrounding the area.  The owner of the property raised the rent to "Fix the Lagoon issue", but raw sewage still runs across the road and into the woods and has for YEARS!  Mr. Fugate should have to fix this issue and clean up the areas affected by his greed and carelessness.
OTHER_FOLLOWUP_TEXT: Forwarded information to MDNR (SWRO) for followup.  Also spoke with Wally Miller of the SWRO.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT:
Received complaint through EPA's website.  The complaint stated that an individual was digging out the creek and changing the course of the waterway.  Mr. Breckenridge did not provide enough information to pinpoint the exact location of complaint. I spoke with Debra Woodward with the Army Corps of Engineers, and she asked that I forward the email. She will try and see if she can locate the potential violation.
OTHER_FOLLOWUP_TEXT: Emailed the individual asking for additional information, and contacted the Army Corps of Engineers.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Approximately 1180 lbs of anhydrous ammonia were released to the atmosphere when vandals left a valve open on a nurse tank.
Approximately 720 gallons of sulfuric acid were discharged onto the ground from a truck due to an accident.

Individual was driving west bound on Interstate 80 in Des Moines and noticed Bob's John's Septic Tank and Mobile truck at 3123 Delaware Avenue tilt up its truck to the right on the side of the building and dump material out into a creek.  Time of discharge was at 7:51 a.m. in the morning (today).  This is the second time this individual has noticed dumping events at this place.  They did not believe this was a legal practice.
OTHER_FOLLOWUP_TEXT: Am forwarding this complaint to the Field Office #5 for follow-up for action.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Approximately 1500 lbs of anhydrous ammonia were released from a storage tank from a valve opened during an attempted theft.

Complainant alleges that discharge of waste from an apparent oil production site into a small stream is killing vegetation, primarily evergreen trees, for more than one mile downstream of the site.  The site may be disguised as an oil prduction stie and could be connected to a threat to national security.
Directions: Please contact the office of Dennis Blair, inform him of my location and THEN contact the Deputy Director at Langley.  Drive west from Kincaid, KS for one mile and you will notice the dying and/or dead vegetation.  Turn left (North) on the county road toward Selma and you will see yellow buildings and oil pumps which are associated with the toxic release.
OTHER_FOLLOWUP_TEXT: Referred complaint to KDHE SEDO (David Stutt) and the KDHE central office (Mike Tate) for follow-up.
